prs.title: Async import of the appStore packages

review_comments.body:
[P0] Async forEach means reschedule deletions aren’t awaited

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` won’t wait for `getCalendar()`/`deleteEvent()`/`deleteMeeting()` to finish, and errors from those promises won’t be caught by the `try/catch`. This can send the reschedule email / return success while external calendar/video artifacts remain. Switch to `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

[P0] Async forEach means reschedule deletions aren’t awaited

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` won’t wait for `getCalendar()`/`deleteEvent()`/`deleteMeeting()` to finish, and errors from those promises won’t be caught by the `try/catch`. This can send the reschedule email / return success while external calendar/video artifacts remain. Switch to `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a `for...of` loop.

[P0] forEach + async drops awaits and errors

The new `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` does not await the async callback, so the calendar/video deletions run fire-and-forget and any failures won’t be caught by surrounding control flow. This can let the mutation return/succeed before external events are actually deleted. Collect promises with `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or use a `for...of` loop with `await`.

reviews.body: Async-loading appStore looks broadly correct, but a few call sites now use `forEach(async ...)`, which does not await external calendar/video deletions and can swallow failures. Fixing these async-iteration bugs should be prioritized to avoid leaving orphaned external events and to ensure errors propagate correctly.

review_comments.body:
[P1] Missing type guard before calling string methods on `backupCode`

The handler calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` without validating that `backupCode` is a string. A malformed JSON body (e.g. `backupCode: null`/number/object) will throw a TypeError and turn into a 500. Validate `typeof backupCode === 'string' && backupCode.length > 0` (and normalize) before using it.

[P1] Backup codes blob URL is never revoked (memory leak)

`URL.createObjectURL()` is used to build `backupCodesUrl`, but that URL is only revoked when a new URL is created; it is not revoked on modal close/reset or component unmount. Revoke it in `resetState()` and/or add a `useEffect` cleanup that calls `URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)` when the URL changes/unmounts.

[P1] Missing type guard before calling string methods on `credentials.backupCode`

The authorize flow calls `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` without ensuring it is a string. While typical form submissions provide strings, unexpected credential shapes can cause a runtime TypeError. Add a guard (e.g. `if (typeof credentials.backupCode !== 'string') throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode);`) before using it.

reviews.body: Backup code support looks good overall; the main issues are a couple of hardening gaps (type-guard `backupCode` inputs before calling string methods in both the API handler and NextAuth authorize) and a small but concrete resource leak from an unreclaimed `createObjectURL()` URL in the enable-2FA modal.

prs.title: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

review_comments.body:
[P0] Potential crash when destinationCalendar is empty

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is derived from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so when destination calendars are missing/empty it becomes `undefined`. The subsequent access `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw at runtime, which would break the booking flow for Meet location events without a destination calendar configured. Guard with optional chaining (e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) or an explicit null/length check before reading `integration`.

[P1] Collective team member destination calendars can be dropped when primary destinationCalendar is null

For COLLECTIVE team events, `teamDestinationCalendars` are gathered from other hosts, but `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then silently no-ops, so team members' destination calendars never get included in that case. Initialize `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (instead of `null`) when you intend to append team calendars, or ensure it is an array before pushing.

[P1] deleteEvent fallback calendarId selection can delete from the wrong calendar

The `calendarId` selection mirrors the same flawed logic as updateEvent: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares to `undefined/null` and will never match. This makes `calendarId` fall back to `primary`, which risks deleting the event from the organizer's primary calendar instead of the intended destination calendar. Use the first destination calendar externalId as the fallback when `externalCalendarId` isn't provided.

[P1] updateEvent selects calendarId using a fallback that can never match

The expression `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is logically flawed: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the fallback branch searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. `=== undefined/null`), which won't match any real destination calendar. This can leave `selectedCalendar` undefined and cause the update to target the wrong calendar (or fail). The likely intended fallback is the first destination calendar's `externalId` (e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`).

[P1] updateAllCalendarEvents can call updateEvent with an undefined credential

In the `reference.credentialId` branch, you attempt to resolve `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials` and fall back to a DB lookup, but if the credential isn't found (or the record lacks `app.slug`) `credential` can remain undefined. The code then unconditionally does `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))`, which can crash when `updateEvent` reads fields off the credential. Add an `if (!credential) { ... }` guard (similar to `createAllCalendarEvents`) before calling `updateEvent`.

reviews.body: There are several concrete correctness issues in the refactor: a runtime crash when Meet is selected with no destination calendar, updateAllCalendarEvents potentially calling updateEvent with an undefined credential, and Google Calendar update/delete deriving an undefined calendarId (and delete potentially falling back to primary). Additionally, collective host destination calendars can be dropped when the primary destinationCalendar is null.

prs.title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

review_comments.body:
[P1] One cancellation failure prevents deleting any cancelled reminders

The try/catch wraps the entire cancellation loop and the final `Promise.all`. If a single `client.request` throws (transient SendGrid/network error), the code jumps to catch and none of the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` operations run, leaving already-cancelled reminders in the DB and retried every run. Handle errors per-reminder (or ensure deletes for successful cancellations run even if one cancellation fails) so partial failures don’t block cleanup.

[P0] immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves reminder row unchanged

When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the SendGrid scheduled send and then returns without updating/deleting the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row. Call sites use `immediateDelete` (e.g. workflow deletion / booking reschedule) and no longer delete reminders in Prisma, so this can leave reminders looking still `scheduled` and never eligible for the `cancelled` cleanup path. Consider deleting the row (or at least setting `cancelled=true`) in the `immediateDelete` branch as well.

[P1] Unawaited async work in forEach when cancelling edited-step reminders

`remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` starts async cancellation/update work but nothing awaits these promises. In serverless/request-scoped execution this can race with subsequent scheduling/response completion, leaving old reminders not reliably cancelled. Use `await Promise.all(remindersToUpdate.map(...))` (or a `for...of` with `await`) to ensure cancellations complete deterministically.

reviews.body: Main correctness gaps are around reminder cleanup determinism: `immediateDelete` cancels SendGrid but can leave DB rows unchanged, the email-reminder cleanup loop aborts all deletions on a single cancellation failure, and one cancellation loop launches async work without awaiting it, making cancellations unreliable under request-scoped execution.

prs.title: Advanced date override handling and timezone compatibility improvements

review_comments.body:
[P1] Working-hours bounds check uses slotStartTime for both start and end

In the working-hours validation, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime`, so `end` is never the actual slot end. This can allow slots whose duration extends past `workingHour.endTime` to be treated as within bounds. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime` (and keep start from `slotStartTime`) so the entire slot is validated against working hours.

[P0] Dayjs object reference comparison always fails

The date override check compares two Dayjs objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`), which is reference equality and will never be true because each `dayjs()` call creates a new object. This breaks the intended zero-duration override handling and can incorrectly reject/accept slots. Use value comparison instead, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(...).isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(...))` (or compare `.valueOf()`/`.toISOString()`).

reviews.body: Found two concrete correctness issues in the new availability logic: a Dayjs `===` comparison that can never be true, and a working-hours bounds check that computes the end from the start time. Fixing those should prevent incorrect slot acceptance/rejection around date overrides and working-hours boundaries.

prs.title: OAuth credential sync and app integration enhancements

review_comments.body:
[P1] Dummy refresh_token assignment breaks refresh flows

When `refresh_token` is missing, the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token", which will later be treated as a real token and cause confusing auth failures. Instead, either keep the existing stored refresh token (passed in by caller), or throw/handle providers that don't return refresh_token on refresh.

[P1] Missing try/catch around decrypt + JSON.parse

`symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` can throw on malformed input; currently this will bubble as a 500. Wrap decryption/parsing in try/catch and return a 400 with a generic error so invalid payloads don’t crash the route.

[P1] Refreshed Salesforce tokens not used for new Connection

After refreshing and persisting the new token, the `jsforce.Connection` is still created from the pre-refresh `credentialKey` values, so it may continue using an expired access token/instance URL. Use `accessTokenParsed.data` (or the merged updated key) when constructing the connection.

[P0] Broken Zod schema for token responses

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` keys, which evaluates to a literal string (e.g. "ZodString") rather than matching arbitrary response keys; this will not validate real OAuth token payloads. Use `.passthrough()`/`.catchall(z.unknown())` and explicitly model known fields (e.g. `access_token`, `expires_in`/`expiry_date`) or use `z.record(z.unknown())` + refinement.

[P0] Saving SafeParseResult instead of credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns a Zod safe-parse result object `{ success, data }`, but the code stores that wrapper as `key` in Prisma instead of `key.data`. This will corrupt the credential `key` shape in the DB and likely break later reads/parses. Use the parsed `data` payload when persisting.

[P0] prisma is used without import

This file calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`, which will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime during token refresh. Add the missing import.

reviews.body: There are several concrete correctness issues in the new OAuth refresh plumbing: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` has a broken schema and its SafeParseResult return value is being persisted as a credential key in at least one call site. The Salesforce refresh path also has a missing `prisma` import and doesn't actually use the refreshed tokens when constructing the connection, and the new webhook route should defensively handle decrypt/JSON parse failures.

prs.title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

review_comments.body:
[P1] retryCount cleanup can delete non-SMS reminders

The `deleteMany` adds an `OR` branch for `retryCount > 1` without also scoping it to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Because `WorkflowReminder.method` can be EMAIL/SMS/WHATSAPP, this SMS scheduler endpoint would delete any reminder type that happens to have `retryCount > 1`, which is unintended data loss. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that OR branch (or wrap the OR under a top-level `method: SMS` constraint) so only SMS reminders are affected.

reviews.body: One cleanup-query issue: the new `retryCount > 1` delete condition is not scoped to `method: SMS`, so it can delete non-SMS workflow reminders when their retryCount exceeds 1.

prs.title: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

review_comments.body:
[P0] Team admin/owner authorization check is incorrect (&& instead of ||)

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` currently requires the user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner, which will incorrectly deny legitimate team admins. Replace the `&&` with `||` (or just call a single helper that checks for either role) so admins or owners can add guests as intended.

[P1] Possible server error when booking.userId is null

The organizer lookup uses `booking.userId || 0` and then `findFirstOrThrow`. If `booking.userId` is null, this queries for `id: 0` and throws, resulting in an unexpected 500 rather than a controlled TRPC error. Add an explicit guard for missing `booking.userId` (and return a meaningful TRPCError) before querying.

[P2] Guest email blacklist check can be bypassed via casing

Blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase, but input guest emails are compared without normalization. A blacklisted address like `blocked@example.com` can slip through by submitting a different case variant. Lowercase (or otherwise normalize) `guest` before comparing against `blacklistedGuestEmails`.

[P1] Empty email fields break validation and prevent submitting valid emails

The dialog initializes `multiEmailValue` as `[""]` and allows adding more empty fields. `handleAdd` validates the raw array, so a mix like `["valid@test.com", ""]` fails `z.string().email()` and blocks adding guests even though there is at least one valid address. Filter out empty/whitespace-only strings before validation/mutation (and consider trimming) to avoid false validation failures.

[P2] Validation error can persist when dialog is dismissed via overlay

`isInvalidEmail` is only reset on Cancel, but `Dialog` can also be closed via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking outside). If a user previously triggered the error, closing/reopening via the overlay will keep showing the stale error state. Reset `isInvalidEmail` when the dialog transitions from open to closed.

[P2] Email sender name ignores EMAIL_FROM_NAME configuration

This template sets `from` using `APP_NAME`, while other email templates use `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` (which allows overriding the sender name via env). Using `APP_NAME` here makes sender naming inconsistent and ignores the configured `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` value.

reviews.body: Validated 6 actionable issues: team-role authorization currently blocks admins, missing booking.userId can throw unexpectedly, blacklist checks are case-bypassable, the dialog can fail validation due to empty fields / stale error state, and the organizer email sender name should use EMAIL_FROM_NAME for consistency.

prs.title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

review_comments.body:
[P1] UI may show stale cache timestamp after delete

After `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` succeeds, the component only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess`, but it does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. If the parent `onSuccess` doesn't refetch, `cacheUpdatedAt` can remain displayed even though the cache rows were deleted; invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query on success/settled to keep the UI consistent.

[P1] macOS-specific sed -i syntax will fail on Linux

The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is BSD/macOS syntax. On Linux (GNU sed), this will error and the env var won't be updated; use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm -f ...` or branch on OS) so the script works in CI/dev environments that run Linux.

reviews.body: Found 3 actionable issues: the SelectedCalendar timestamp 'touch' is currently a no-op (and may error), the cache-delete UI doesn't invalidate connectedCalendars so it can remain stale, and the webhook test script uses macOS-only sed flags that break on Linux.

Correction: the `SelectedCalendar.updateManyByCredentialId(..., {})` line is not necessarily a no-op because Prisma `@updatedAt` can be set automatically on updates. Remaining actionable items: invalidate/refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` after `deleteCache`, and make `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` portable (GNU vs BSD `sed -i`).
